Re: Testimony in Support of LD 51, An Act to Increase Oversight of Fatalities of and Serious Injuries to Adults Subject to Public Guardianship
Dear Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services:
My name is Barrett Littlefield and I am a senior staff attorney at Disability Rights Maine. DRM is Maine's designated Protection and Advocacy Agency, and our mission is to advance justice and equality by enforcing rights and expanding opportunities for people with disabilities in Maine. Thank you for this opportunity to provide testimony in support of LD 51.
Passage of LD 51 will ensure the meaningful inclusion of elder Mainers and adults with developmental disabilities who receive Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) and/or are subject to public guardianship on Maine's Aging and Disability Mortality Review Panel. The Mortality Review Panel is incomplete and their work hindered without the assistance of a member with lived experience relevant to the Panel's mission: the possible prevention of serious injury and death of adult recipients of Home and Community-Based Services and adults subject to public guardianship. This is a matter of both health equity and common sense. Persons with said lived experience offer a vital perspective, without which the Mortality Review Panel is unable to comprehensively fulfill their duty to identify factors contributing to the mortality of Maine elders and individuals with developmental disabilities and the larger strengths and weaknesses of Maine's system of support for said persons. Most importantly, adults receiving elder and/or developmental support services can make connections between their own lived experience, structural determinants of health, and information concerning the deaths or serious injury of similarly-situated peers that could contribute

to the prevention of serious injury or death in the future. Without the membership of an adult who receives the aforementioned support services, the Mortality Review Panel is denied the ability to fully understand the contexts of serious injuries and deaths under their review and, ultimately, to document essential prevention recommendations identifiable therein. In sum, LD 51 presents both an opportunity to better support Maine's Aging and Disability Mortality Review Panel in their current work and the greater possibility of forestalling preventable deaths in the future.
Additionally, DRM recommends the bill be amended to provide a community participation stipend to the adult service recipient member of the Mortality Review Panel whose time on the Panel is not otherwise compensated. Similar to the stipend provided to certain members of Maine's Maternal, Fetal, and Infant Mortality Review Panel, the community participation stipend would be available for participation in Panel meetings to the member with lived experience who, unlike other Panel members, would not be participating representing their professional role or expertise. Similarly, the stipend would aid in recruitment of and allow for the full participation of a new Mortality Review Panel member with lived experience.
For the foregoing reasons, DRM supports LD 51, and we urge this Committee to vote ought to pass as amended. Thank you for your time and consideration.

AARP Maine Testimony in support of LD 51 An Act to Increase Oversight of Fatalities of and Serious Injuries to Adults Subject to Public Guardianship
Greetings Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and members of the Committee On Health and Human Services. My name is Bridget Quinn, Associate State Director of Advocacy and Outreach for AARP Maine.
AARP is the nation's largest nonprofit, nonpartisan organization dedicated to empowering Americans 50 and older to choose how they live as they age. On behalf of our nearly 200,000 members statewide, thank you for the opportunity to share testimony today. We thank Representative Shagoury for bringing forward this bill and will be offering testimony in support of LD 51.
LD 51 will require the Aging and Disability Mortality Review Panel to expand their membership to include a member of the general public with lived experience as an adult receiving services among other members. LD 51 also requires the Panel to review all deaths and serious injuries of adults subject to public guardianship regardless of whether they are enrolled in a home or community-based service program.
The goals of LD 51 are admirable and seek to expand protection to some of our most vulnerable Mainers. AARP continuously fights to support Maine's vulnerable seniors who rely on legal guardians and others to help them make vital decisions. While Maine has the "gold standard" of guardianship laws in the Uniform Guardianship, Conservatorship, and Other Protective Arrangements Act, the very nature of guardianship means that we all need to be vigilant to ensure that vulnerable seniors are not abused, bad guardians are held accountable, and the courts can do their jobs.
While supportive of LD 51, AARP's policies seek to ensure that guardianships should always be an option of last resort. Adults placed under guardianship lose their basic civil liberties. These can include making decisions about where to live, how to spend money, and what medical treatment to receive. We will continue to work with policymakers to ensure Mainers under guardianship are able to maximize their independence while also receiving the protections of guardianship. There is still work to be done.
LD 51 is a step in the right direction to protect Mainers under public guardianship. While

public guardians serve a necessary and important role, their clients are some of our most vulnerable citizens. It directs Maine policy towards protections in line with policy recommendations established by delegates from the National Guardianship Summit. That is why we urge you to support LD 51. Thank you for the opportunity to provide testimony today, if you have further questions for me I can be contacted at bquinn@aarp.org or at 207-272-8563.
Thank you, Bridget Quinn AARP Maine

Re: LD 51 An Act to Increase Oversight of Fatalities of and Serious Injuries to Adults Subject to Public Guardianship
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and members of the Health and Human Services Committee, my name is Cullen Ryan, and I am the Executive Director of Community Housing of Maine or CHOM. I am also the parent of a 28-year-old son with Intellectual/Developmental Disabilities (ID/DD). I serve as Chair of the Maine Coalition for Housing and Quality Services, a coalition of some 4000 people, consisting primarily of parents, that focuses on housing and quality services for people with ID/DD. I also serve as chair of the Maine Developmental Services Oversight and Advisory Board (MDSOAB).
I am testifying in support of LD 51, An Act to Increase Oversight of Fatalities of and Serious Injuries to Adults Subject to Public Guardianship. Under current law, the Aging and Disability Mortality Review Panel reviews deaths of and serious injuries to adults receiving services in home-based and community-based services programs, including participants in those programs who are subject to public guardianship. This bill expands the charge of the panel to review all deaths of and serious injuries to adults subject to public guardianship, whether or not they are enrolled in homebased and community-based services programs. It also amends the membership of the panel.
The original establishment of the Mortality Review Panel was wise and timely. The Mortality Review Panel plays a critical role by reviewing deaths and identifying systemic changes which might have made a difference for the people who unfortunately passed in order to help prevent future instances or serious injury or death. I am pleased to see that Governor Mills is invested in enhancing and expanding this essential panel through this legislation.
This bill includes important improvements to the Mortality Review Panel, including expanding the population scope to include adults under Public Guardianship. This bill would also add to the existing panel, proposing a statutory change to include a medical provider, a representative from Adult Protective Services, and a person with lived experience. All of these additions would serve to improve the effectiveness of the Mortality Review Panel.
Please pass LD 51 so that Maine's Mortality Review Panel can be best poised to review and identify instances of serious injury or death so that Maine is better equipped to prevent them in the future.
Thank you for the opportunity to comment.

Testimony of the Office of Aging and Disability Services
Maine Department of Health and Human Services
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services
In support of LD 51, An Act to Increase Oversight of Fatalities of and Serious Injuries to Adults
Subject to Public Guardianship
Sponsor: Representative Shagoury Hearing Date: February 4, 2025
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health
and Human Services, my name is Gina Googins, and I serve as the Associate Director of Adult
Protective Services of the Office of Aging and Disability Services (OADS) in the Maine Department
of Health and Human Services. I am here today to testify in support of LD 51, An Act to Increase
Oversight ofFatalities ofand Serious Injuries to Adults Subject to Public Guardianship. This is a
Department bill, and we are grateful to Rep. Shagoury for sponsoring it.
Under current law, the Aging and Disability Mortality Review Panel reviews deaths of and serious
injuries to adults receiving services under MaineCare-funded Home and Community Based Services -or HCBS -- programs, including participants in those programs who are subject to public guardianship.
This bill expands the charge of the Panel to review all deaths and serious injuries for adults subject to
public guardianship, whether or not they are enrolled in HCBS programs. It also amends the
membership of the Panel to include a person within the Department responsible for Adult Protective
Services, a member of the general public with lived experience as an adult receiving services, and a primary health care provider who is licensed under Title 32, Chapter 36 or 48.
The Aging and Disability Mortality Review Panel was established by Maine law in 2021 (PL 2021, c.
398. PT. MMMM, �2) to review the patterns of death and serious injury to all Maine adults
participating in HCBS programs. The Panel is required to meet at least four times per year and reports annually to the Legislature and DHHS Commissioner. The Panel has a full time Coordinator located at the Maine Centers for Disease Control (CDC). Maine CDC was consulted on this bill and supports it.
Individuals subject to public guardianship share many similarities to HCBS waiver participants, and in fact 39% of individuals receiving public guardianship services also receive HCBS. Given the lower
involvement of natural supports and the higher risk of abuse, neglect and exploitation among
individuals subject to public guardianship, the Department believes that all deaths and serious injuries
among them should have this level of review. The Department further believes that the addition of the three recommended Panel members will bring a set of experiences, knowledge and ideas to the table that will make for a more informed and robust Panel.
Thank you for your time and attention. I would be happy to answer any questions you may have and to make myself available for questions at the work session.

Good afternoon, Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and members of the Joint
Standing Committee on Health and Human Services.
My name is John Brautigam, and I am here today on behalf of Legal Services for Maine
Elders. LSE provides free legal help for Mainers aged 60 and older when their basic human
needs are at stake.
Under current law, when a person receiving home-based or community-based services dies or is seriously harmed, the circumstances may be reviewed by the Aging and Disability
Mortality Review Panel. LD 51 would extend the work of the Aging and Disability
Mortality Review Panel to include people in public guardianship even if they are not receiving HBCS.
LSE supports this change. People in guardianship are a special class, requiring special care
and attention. The occurrence of an unusual death or serious injury of any person under
guardianship provides an-opportunity to assess what is working well and what may not be
working in the guardianship program.
Currently, the Aging and Disability Mortality Review Panel only conducts a review when
the person who dies or is injured is in Home and Community Based Services. There is likely an historical reason why the panel's review is focused on those receiving HCBS services. But the scope need not be limited. LD 51 sets up a more inclusive framework. Under the
bill, the death or injury of Q1 person under guardianship could be reviewed by the panel,
even if the person is living in a nursing home or residential care setting, or if living in a personal residence without HCBS. This makes sense.

Testimony of Laura Cordes In Support of
LD 51 An Act to Increase Oversight of Fatalities of and Serious Injuries to Adults Subject to Public Guardianship
February 4, 2025
Good afternoon, Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services.
My name is Laura Cordes. I am the Executive Director for the Maine Association for Community Service Providers (MACSP), the statewide association of nearly one hundred agencies that deliver person-centered educational, vocational, residential, and community supports, as well as specialized services and care to a diverse population of Maine children and adults who have either intellectual disabilities, autism spectrum disorder, or brain injuries, so that they may live full and meaningful lives in the community.
Together our members deliver services to more than 5000 adults and 2000 children with an estimated workforce of 9,000 direct service professionals.
MACSP is in support of LD 51, An Act to Increase Oversight of Fatalities of and Serious Injuries to Adults Subject to Public Guardianship. This legislation is essential to ensuring the safety, dignity, and well-being of one of our most vulnerable populations--adults under public guardianship.
Maine has already demonstrated a commitment to reviewing and understanding the factors that contribute to deaths and serious injuries through existing mortality review panels. The Aging and Disability Mortality Review Panel and the Maine Maternal, Fetal, and Infant Mortality Review Panel serve as critical mechanisms for analyzing mortality trends, identifying weaknesses in systems of care, and making recommendations to improve health outcomes. However, there is currently no similar oversight mechanism dedicated to adults subject to public guardianship--a group that often lacks the advocacy and support systems that others may have.
We applaud the Department and Representative Shagoury for introducing this legislation which will expand the scope of the Aging and Disability Mortality Review Panel to include this population. Adults under public guardianship are among the most vulnerable in our state, often experiencing complex medical conditions, disabilities, and limited autonomy. Without proper oversight, systemic failures and preventable tragedies may go unnoticed, and opportunities for improvement may be lost.
LD 51 seeks to address this gap by implementing a structured review process for fatalities and serious injuries, ensuring that every death or injury is not just a statistic but a lesson for improving care and protection.

It also aligns with Maine's existing commitment to public health and the responsible oversight of vulnerable populations. By adopting this measure, we take another critical step toward ensuring that adults under public guardianship receive the care, protection, and dignity they deserve. I urge this committee to support LD 51 and to move this legislation forward. Thank you for your consideration. Laura Cordes laura.cordes@meacsp.org

Testimony of Marge Kilkelly on Behalf of the Maine Council on Aging to the Committee on
Health and Human Services
In Favor of LD 51 - An Act to Increase Oversight of Fatalities of and Serious Injuries to Adults Subject to
Public Guardianship
Submitted February 4, 2025
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and the members of the Committee on Health and Human Services.
My name is Marge Kilkelly, and I am a Policy Consultant for the Maine Council on Aging (MCOA). The MCOA is a broad, multidisciplinary network of over 135 organizations, businesses, municipalities, and older community members working to ensure we can all live healthy, engaged, and secure lives with choices and opportunities as we age at home and in community settings.
I am testifying in favor of LD 51 - An Act to Increase Oversight of Fatalities of and Serious Injuries to Adults Subject to Public Guardianship
In 2021 the Legislature wisely created the Aging and Disability Mortality Review Panel (ADMRP) to review cases of severe injury or death of adults receiving home or community based services. The information gathered is used to identify the strengths and weaknesses of the care systems and recommend changes in law, rules, training, policy and procedures which would strengthen the system and protection of adults. LD 51 expands the panel's scope to include adults under public guardianship.
Incapacitated persons under public guardianship are often more vulnerable than some of the individuals currently covered by the ADMRP. While public guardianship is a critical service for some individuals; a public guardian is not typically a family member or close friend, and may not have the same level of understanding about the individual's personal preferences, values, and life goals. Public guardian agencies often have large caseloads and limited oversight which leads to less time understanding each individuals needs and an increased risk of exploitation. We applaud the Department for taking the extra step to learn how public guardianship processes can be made better by studying deaths and serious injuries of public wards. We also support changes in the composition of the ADMRP to include a person within the Department responsible for Adult Protective Services, a member of the general public with lived experience as an adult receiving services, and a primary health care provider.
I urge you to act in support of LD 51.

LD 51: An Act to Increase Oversight of Fatalities of and Serious Injuries to Adults Subject
to Public Guardianship

Nicole Marchesi
Maine Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services
February 4, 2025
Good afternoon, Senator lngwersen, Representative Meyer, and members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Health and Human Services. My name is Nicole Marchesi. I am the Public Policy Advocate for the Maine Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program.
As you know, the Ombudsman Program serves older and disabled adults who are residents of nursing homes, residential care, assisted living and recipients of adult day services and home
care services.
We are pleased to present testimony in support of this legislation that proposes the expansion
of the charge of the Aging and Disability Mortality Review Panel to review all deaths of and serious injuries to adults subject to public guardianship, whether or not they are enrolled in
home and community -based services programs. It also expands the membership of the panel.
Ombudsman Program staff serves on the panel. lt has been particularly helpful that the Aging and Disability Mortality Review Panel Coordinator, Anne Lovegren MSN, RN, FNP-BC has an
extensive medical background and has completed a nationally certified training program for conducting critical incident, including death, investigations. As such, she is well prepared for
her important role. Additionally, Dr. Lauren Michalakes MD serves on the panel as
representative of the DHHS, Office of Aging and Disability Services. Dr. Michalakes is an internist with more than twenty years' experience. Her background has added expertise that has been very helpful to the work of the panel. The broad range of stakeholders serving on the
panel has enhanced its effectiveness.

Expansion of the panel to include a person responsible for adult protective services, a member
with lived experience as an adult receiving services, and a primary health care provider will be
beneficial to the panel.
As the panel considers deaths and serious injuries to individuals under public guardianship, the input of a representative from DHHS, Adult Protective Services concerning their policies and practices regarding visitation and oversight of adults under public guardianship will aid in conducting a comprehensive review. This will also be helpful in consideration of potential changes to improve oversight and the wellbeing of individuals under public guardianship.
Thank you for your consideration.
10032665:
Maine Developmental Disabilities Council
February 11, 2025
Dear Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services: please accept this testimony in support of LD 51, An Act to Increase Oversight of Fatalities of and Serious Injuries to Adults Subject to Public Guardianship.
The Maine Developmental Disabilities Council (MDDC) works in partnership with people with disabilities, parents, advocates, and policy makers to promote independence, integration, and inclusion of all people with disabilities through advocacy, capacity building, and systems change throughout the state of Maine and on the national level.
Under the federal Developmental Disabilities Assistance and Bill of Rights Act of 2000, MDDC is required to ensure that individuals with developmental disabilities of all ages and their families participate in the design of, and have access to, needed community services, individualized support, and other forms of assistance that promote self-determination, independence, productivity, integration, and inclusion in all facets of family and community life. MDDC is committed to creating a Maine in which all people are valued and respected because we believe communities are stronger when everyone is included.
MDDC appreciates Maine's commitment to systemic improvement by examining the circumstances that contribute to deaths and serious injuries through the Aging and Disability Mortality Review Panel. We particularly appreciate several items of this proposal, including
o Extending oversight to adults subject to public guardianship. Consider that reporting includes numbers and demographics of people under public guardianship.
o Inclusion of a member with lived experience. Consider including stipend for participation. o Inclusion of person adult protective services, especially as APS seems to be siloed from
the entities overseeing services.
We appreciate the Department and Representative Shagoury for introducing this legislation.
Rachel Dyer Maine Developmental Disabilities Council.

10032021:
Richard Estabrook Brunswick Maine LD 51
Due to another commitment pertaining to persons with intellectual disabilities or autism in Maine I was not able to attend the public hearing on LD 51 today. I am writing in order to urge passage of the LD 51, principally because of the increased oversight it will provide to persons under public guardianship. I well remember the death of Norman F., a person with intellectual disabilities, who was under public guardianship. Norman's full name was mentioned in the press but I have chosen not to use his last name. He died in August 2019. I have always believed that the state guardian fumbled in his duties in this case by not attending a person centered planning meeting prior to Norman moving to a new residence. Specifically adding "adults subject to public guardianship" to the jurisdiction of the Oversight board is a step in the right direction. Too often there is a conflict of interest, or at least the appearance of a conflict of interest, when a person under DHHS guardianship has a catastrophic event occur. It is a fox guarding the henhouse problem. LD 51 addresses this issue. Thank you for your attention to this.
10031857:
Richard Mardoian South Portland LD 51
I so not support LD 51, "An Act to Increase Oversight of Fatalities of and Serious Injuries to Adults subject to public guardianship."
Ensuring the rights to Life, Liberty, and the Pursuit of happiness is a fundamental right guaranteed by the constitution of the United States of America. The very public guardianship abuse suffered by Ms. Britney Jean Spears of Kentwood Louisiana, highlights how states nefarious actors colluded to strip Britney of her constitutional rights.
In the event that this could occur in the Great State of Maine, a robust Oversight procedure is a must.
I do not support LD51, "An Act To Increase Oversight of Fatalities of and Serious Injuries to Adults Subject to Public Gaurdianship," because I believe it makes the investigation process less transparent if misconduct is found to have occurred and it ought not pass.
